title: CoherentFormalModulesCokernelClosure
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. The property of being a coherent adic inverse system [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] is closed under cokernels in the ambient category of inverse systems of $\mathcal O_X$-modules: for every map between two such systems, the vertex of every colimiting cokernel cofork is again such a system.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), first sentence of the proof, termwise cokernels (details omitted)

proof.text: Ambient cokernels of inverse systems are computed termwise. For $\alpha:F\to G$, coherence of $C_n=\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_n)$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth]. Naturality of $\alpha$ induces transitions of $C$. On affine sections [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] identifies $C_n$ with $G_n/\alpha_n(F_n)$ and gives surjective quotient projections.

The ideal-power annihilation of $G_n$ passes to its quotient $C_n$. The transition of $F$ is surjective, and the transition on $G$ has kernel $I^nG_{n+1}$ in positive-level notation. Thus $\alpha_{n+1}(F_{n+1})$ maps onto $\alpha_n(F_n)$, and $C_{n+1}/I^nC_{n+1}\cong G_{n+1}/(\alpha_{n+1}(F_{n+1})+I^nG_{n+1})\cong C_n$. Its composite with the quotient projection is precisely the induced transition. Apply the affine ideal-product and quotient formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] and the tilde/Gamma identification [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] to obtain the sheaf conditions. In Lean level $\operatorname{op} n$ represents positive level $n+1$.

Every colimiting ambient cokernel cofork is uniquely isomorphic to the termwise one. Its vertex therefore satisfies the same three object conditions. This is exactly closure under cokernels, without assuming abelianness of the formal subcategory.
